`design/mockups/ui/interact.js`:

```js
// Interaction and transitions (motion.rs in the game does the same):
// - go(): another screen. The current one tunes out, the next tunes in. Between menu pages
//   only the page and the assistant swap; the frame stays and the selection slides.
// - a sliding selection (.ind) in every list and chip group;
// - choices burst once, steppers roll their value, buy categories and items swap in place.
const T_OUT = 180;

// Put the sliding selection under the chosen row or chip. `animate` false snaps it.
function placeInd(group, animate = true) {
  const ind = group.querySelector(':scope > .ind');
  if (!ind) return;
  const on = group.querySelector(':scope > .on');
  if (!animate) ind.style.transition = 'none';
  if (on) Object.assign(ind.style, { opacity: 1, transform: `translate(${on.offsetLeft}px, ${on.offsetTop}px)`, width: `${on.offsetWidth}px`, height: `${on.offsetHeight}px` });
  else ind.style.opacity = 0;
  if (!animate) { void ind.offsetWidth; ind.style.transition = ''; }
}

// After new markup lands: sliding selections in place, setting rows staggered.
function decorate(root) {
  for (const g of root.querySelectorAll('.chips')) {
    if (g.querySelector(':scope > .chip') && !g.querySelector(':scope > .ind')) g.prepend(Object.assign(document.createElement('i'), { className: 'ind' }));
  }
  root.querySelectorAll('.srow').forEach((r, i) => { r.classList.add('tune'); r.style.setProperty('--i', i + 1); });
  const groups = root.querySelectorAll('.nav, .chips');
  for (const g of groups) placeInd(g, false);
  // chip widths change once the web fonts arrive
  document.fonts?.ready.then(() => { for (const g of groups) placeInd(g, false); });
}

// Swap a container's content: the old content tunes out, the new tunes in.
function swap(el, html, then) {
  el.classList.add('out');
  setTimeout(() => {
    el.classList.remove('out');
    el.innerHTML = html;
    if (el.classList.contains('tune')) { el.classList.remove('tune'); void el.offsetWidth; el.classList.add('tune'); }
    decorate(el);
    speakAll(el);
    then?.();
  }, T_OUT);
}

function restart(el, cls) { el.classList.remove(cls); void el.offsetWidth; el.classList.add(cls); }

function go(k) {
  if (k === current || busy) return;
  const a = SCREENS[current], b = SCREENS[k];
  history.replaceState(null, '', '#' + k);
  busy = true;
  if (a.menu && b.menu) {
    // Same frame: slide the selection, swap the page and the assistant.
    const nav = stage.querySelector('.nav');
    nav.querySelectorAll(':scope > .item').forEach(i => i.classList.toggle('on', i.dataset.go === k));
    placeInd(nav);
    const on = nav.querySelector('.item.on .h2');
    if (on) restart(on, 'pop');   // back on the main menu nothing is selected
    current = k;
    for (const t of tabs.children) t.setAttribute('aria-current', t.dataset.k === k);
    note.textContent = b.note;
    swap(stage.querySelector('#extra'), b.extra());
    const pg = stage.querySelector('#page');
    if (b.menu === 'Main') {
      // back to the straight menu: everything swings flat, the page leaves
      flatten3d(stage);
      pg.classList.add('out');
      setTimeout(() => { pg.classList.remove('out'); pg.classList.add('empty'); pg.innerHTML = ''; busy = false; }, T_OUT);
      return;
    }
    if (a.menu === 'Main') {
      // from the straight menu: the page comes in and everything swings into 3D
      pg.innerHTML = b.page(); pg.classList.remove('empty'); decorate(pg); restart(pg, 'tune');
      setTimeout(() => { open3d(stage); busy = false; }, 30);
      return;
    }
    swing(pg, true);
    swap(pg, b.page(), () => { busy = false; swing(pg, false); });
    return;
  }
  stage.classList.add('out');
  setTimeout(() => { stage.classList.remove('out'); show(k); busy = false; }, T_OUT);
}
let busy = false;

// Step a value like "2.40", "80%", "300" or "4".
function step(v, dir) {
  const n = parseFloat(v), pct = v.endsWith('%'), dec = v.includes('.');
  const d = dec ? 0.1 : pct ? 5 : n >= 100 ? 10 : 1;
  const x = Math.max(0, n + dir * d);
  return (dec ? x.toFixed(2) : String(Math.round(x))) + (pct ? '%' : '');
}

stage.addEventListener('click', e => {
  const t = e.target;
  const goEl = t.closest('[data-go]');
  if (goEl) return go(goEl.dataset.go);

  // buy: category, then item
  const cat = t.closest('.buycats > .item');
  if (cat) {
    const i = [...cat.parentElement.querySelectorAll(':scope > .item')].indexOf(cat);
    if (i === buyState.cat) return;
    cat.parentElement.querySelectorAll(':scope > .item').forEach((x, j) => x.classList.toggle('on', j === i));
    placeInd(cat.parentElement); restart(cat.querySelector('.h2'), 'pop');
    buyState.cat = i; buyState.sel = 0;
    swap(stage.querySelector('#cards'), buyCards(i, 0));
    swap(stage.querySelector('#details'), buyDetails(i, 0));
    return;
  }
  const card = t.closest('#cards > .card');
  if (card) {
    const i = +card.dataset.item;
    if (i === buyState.sel) return;
    stage.querySelectorAll('#cards > .card').forEach(c => c.classList.toggle('sel', c === card));
    restart(card, 'pop');
    buyState.sel = i;
    swap(stage.querySelector('#details'), buyDetails(buyState.cat, i));
    return;
  }

  // a stepper: roll the value toward the change
  const stepBtn = t.closest('.stepper > .chip');
  if (stepBtn) {
    const v = stepBtn.parentElement.querySelector('.v'), up = stepBtn === stepBtn.parentElement.lastElementChild;
    v.innerHTML = `<span class="${up ? 'roll-up' : 'roll-down'}">${step(v.textContent.trim(), up ? 1 : -1)}</span>`;
    return;
  }
  // a choice in a group: the selection slides to it, it bursts once
  const chip = t.closest('.chips > .chip');
  if (chip && !chip.classList.contains('on')) {
    const g = chip.parentElement;
    g.querySelectorAll(':scope > .chip').forEach(c => c.classList.toggle('on', c === chip));
    placeInd(g); restart(chip, 'pop');
    return;
  }
  // an assistant card: say it again
  const up = t.closest('.uplink[data-ai]');
  if (up) return speak(up, { stay: true });
  // pause menu: Resume closes it; side cards select
  const item = t.closest('.over .nav > .item');
  if (item && item.querySelector('.h2').textContent === 'Resume') return toggle.click();
  const side = t.closest('.over .card');
  if (side) { stage.querySelectorAll('.over .card').forEach(c => c.classList.toggle('sel', c === side)); restart(side, 'pop'); }
});

// 3D: the UI sits on a curved visor. Each part turns toward you by where it sits (left parts
// in from the left, right parts from the right, top and bottom tilt in), hinged on its outer
// edge; `data-depth` pushes a layer back (negative) or forward.
const CURVE_Y = 26, CURVE_X = 18;   // degrees at the screen edges (the HUD)
// Persona-style: the main menu sits straight and flat (no page). Opening something brings its
// page in and swings every part into its 3D place in turn, overshooting a little so it lands
// with weight; Esc swings it all back flat and the page leaves. The HUD takes its curve at once.
// `?p=0..1` freezes the swing part way (stills).
const SETTLE = 820, SETTLE_STAGGER = 70, FLATTEN = 380;
const SETTLE_EASE = 'cubic-bezier(.2, 1.3, .32, 1)', FLATTEN_EASE = 'cubic-bezier(.4, 0, .2, 1)';
function rot(ry, rx, k = 1) {
  return ry || rx ? (Math.abs(ry) > Math.abs(rx) ? `y ${(ry * k).toFixed(1)}deg` : `x ${(rx * k).toFixed(1)}deg`) : 'none';
}
function menuParts(root) { return [...root.querySelectorAll(':scope > *:not(.world):not(script)')]; }
// Put every part k of the way to its 3D place (0 flat, 1 placed), animated or not.
function placeAll(root, k, { dur = 0, ease = SETTLE_EASE, stagger = 0 } = {}) {
  menuParts(root).forEach((el, i) => {
    if (!el.dataset.place) return;
    const [ry, rx, z] = JSON.parse(el.dataset.place);
    const inner = el.matches('[data-tilt="none"]:not(.space):not(.far16)') ? [...el.querySelectorAll('.abs')] : [];
    const t = dur ? `rotate ${dur}ms ${ease} ${i * stagger}ms, translate ${dur}ms ${ease} ${i * stagger}ms` : 'none';
    el.style.transition = t;
    el.style.translate = `0 0 ${(z * k).toFixed(1)}px`;
    el.style.rotate = rot(ry, rx, k);
    for (const n of inner) { n.style.transition = t; n.style.transformOrigin = 'right center'; n.style.rotate = `y ${(-14 * k).toFixed(1)}deg`; }
  });
}
function curve(root) {
  const hud = !!root.querySelector('.hudlayer');
  const parts = hud ? root.querySelectorAll('.hudlayer > .abs:not(.over):not(.scrim):not(.sweep)') : menuParts(root);
  const still = document.body.classList.contains('still');
  const p = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, parseFloat(new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('p') ?? '1')));
  for (const el of parts) {
    if (el.classList.contains('world') || el.classList.contains('over')) continue;
    const r = el.getBoundingClientRect(), b = root.getBoundingClientRect(), k = 1920 / b.width;
    const cx = ((r.left + r.right) / 2 - b.left) * k / 1920 - .5, cy = ((r.top + r.bottom) / 2 - b.top) * k / 1080 - .5;
    const wide = r.width * k > 1500, tall = r.height * k > 900;
    // only the HUD follows the visor curve; menu screens turn only the parts that ask to
    // (`data-tilt="y 12"`)
    const [axis, deg] = (el.dataset.tilt ?? '').split(' ');
    let ry = !hud || wide ? 0 : -cx * 2 * CURVE_Y, rx = !hud || tall ? 0 : cy * 2 * CURVE_X;
    if (axis) { ry = axis === 'y' ? +deg : 0; rx = axis === 'x' ? +deg : 0; }
    const z = parseFloat(el.dataset.depth ?? '0') * 160;
    // HUD: hinged on the side toward the middle, so the outer edge comes toward you (curved
    // visor glass); menus set their own hinge
    el.style.transformOrigin = el.dataset.hinge ?? (Math.abs(ry) >= Math.abs(rx) ? `${cx < 0 ? 'right' : 'left'} center` : `center ${cy < 0 ? 'bottom' : 'top'}`);
    el.dataset.place = JSON.stringify([ry, rx, z]);
  }
  // the HUD doesn't turn part by part: it bends as one surface (visor, below)
  if (hud) return visor(root);
  // a menu page open: shown placed (a still at p), or arrive flat then swing; none: flat
  const open = !!root.querySelector('#page:not(.empty)');
  placeAll(root, open && still ? p : 0);
  if (open && !still) setTimeout(() => placeAll(root, 1, { dur: SETTLE, stagger: SETTLE_STAGGER }), 30);
}
// The HUD seen through a visor: a very slight bulge, the middle swelling toward you and the
// edges leaning back. The game bends the HUD's image with one shader (smooth sampling); here
// each panel takes the same bulge in real 3D, which the browser draws smoothly.
const BULGE_Z = 40, BULGE_Y = 9, BULGE_X = 7;   // px toward you at the middle; degrees at the edges
function visor(root) {
  const b = root.getBoundingClientRect(), k = 1920 / b.width;
  // ?bulge=0..2 scales it (comparison shots)
  const m = parseFloat(new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('bulge') ?? '1');
  for (const el of root.querySelectorAll('.hudlayer > .abs:not(.over):not(.scrim):not(.sweep)')) {
    const r = el.getBoundingClientRect();
    const u = (((r.left + r.right) / 2 - b.left) * k / 1920 - .5) * 2, v = (((r.top + r.bottom) / 2 - b.top) * k / 1080 - .5) * 2;
    if (r.width * k > 1500) continue;
    const r2 = u * u + v * v;
    el.style.transformOrigin = 'center';
    el.style.translate = `0 0 ${(m * BULGE_Z * (1 - r2 / 2)).toFixed(1)}px`;
    // the outer edges lean away: left panels turn their left edge back, top panels their top
    const ax = -v * BULGE_X * m, ay = u * BULGE_Y * m, ang = Math.hypot(ax, ay);
    el.style.rotate = ang ? `${(ax / ang).toFixed(3)} ${(ay / ang).toFixed(3)} 0 ${ang.toFixed(2)}deg` : 'none';
  }
}

// Opening a page from the straight menu, and Esc back to it.
function open3d(root) { placeAll(root, 1, { dur: SETTLE, stagger: SETTLE_STAGGER }); }
function flatten3d(root) { placeAll(root, 0, { dur: FLATTEN, ease: FLATTEN_EASE }); }
// A page swap while open: the page straightens while it swaps, then swings back into place.
function swing(el, flat) {
  if (!el?.dataset.place) return;
  const [ry, rx, z] = JSON.parse(el.dataset.place);
  el.style.transition = flat ? `rotate ${T_OUT}ms ease-in, translate ${T_OUT}ms ease-in` : `rotate ${SETTLE}ms ${SETTLE_EASE}, translate ${SETTLE}ms ${SETTLE_EASE}`;
  el.style.rotate = flat ? 'none' : rot(ry, rx);
  el.style.translate = flat ? '0 0 0' : `0 0 ${z}px`;
}
// Esc: a menu page closes back to the straight main menu.
document.addEventListener('keydown', e => {
  if (e.key === 'Escape' && SCREENS[current]?.menu && SCREENS[current].menu !== 'Main') go('main');
});


```

`design/mockups/ui/rig.js`:

```js
// The face rig: makes every portrait alive (assistant/view.rs mirrors it with sprite layers).
// - Head turn with depth: layers move by different amounts (back hair against the turn, the
//   features and fringe the most) and the head tilts on the neck.
// - Idle: a slow drift and blinks. Talking: the mouth moves and the head nods with it.
// - Moods: each has a pose the head eases into; changing mood glitches in.
// - Personality scales all of it: ChildGBT barely moves, Grumpk and the sister overact.

// yaw (turn, + to her left), pitch (+ down), roll (+ tilt clockwise), in rig units (~degrees).
const POSE = {
  neutral: [0, 0, 0], happy: [2, -2, 5], laughing: [0, -6, 7], smug: [5, -4, -7], shocked: [0, -7, 0],
  thinking: [-7, -4, 8], worried: [-2, 3, -4], sad: [-3, 7, -5], annoyed: [9, 1, -4],
};
const LIVELY = { claudette: .75, childgbt: .25, sister: 1.25, brother: .6, grumpk: 1.35 };
// how far each layer moves per unit of turn / nod
const DEPTH = { 'L-back': -0.35, 'L-skull': 0.4, 'L-feat': 0.95, 'L-front': 0.75 };

const RIGS = new Set();

class Rig {
  constructor(tile) {
    this.tile = tile;
    this.who = tile.dataset.face;
    this.c = getComputedStyle(tile).getPropertyValue('--c').trim();
    this.mood = tile.dataset.mood || 'neutral';
    this.phase = Math.random() * 100;
    this.pose = [0, 0, 0];          // current, eased
    this.kick = [0, 0, 0];          // a short impulse (jolts, bounces)
    this.talking = false;
    this.nextBlink = performance.now() + 800 + Math.random() * 3000;
    this.blinkUntil = 0;
    this.flap = 0;
    this.bind();
    RIGS.add(this);
    tile.rig = this;
  }
  bind() {
    const q = c => [...this.tile.querySelectorAll('.' + c)];
    this.g = Object.fromEntries(Object.keys(DEPTH).map(k => [k, q(k)]));
    this.head = q('L-head');
    this.eyes = q('L-eyes'); this.shut = q('L-shut'); this.mouth = q('L-mouth'); this.talk = q('L-talk');
  }
  render() {
    this.tile.innerHTML = faceSvg(this.who, this.c, this.mood, false, this.tile.offsetWidth < 100 ? TILE_VIEW : undefined);
    this.bind();
  }
  setMood(m) {
    if (m === this.mood) return;
    this.mood = m;
    this.tile.dataset.mood = m;
    this.render();
    restart(this.tile, 'pop');                       // the change glitches in
    if (m === 'shocked') this.kick = [0, -8, 0];     // a jolt back
    if (m === 'laughing') this.kick = [0, -4, 6];
  }
  setWho(w, mood = this.mood) { this.who = w; this.mood = mood; this.tile.dataset.mood = mood; this.render(); restart(this.tile, 'pop'); }
  step(now, dt) {
    const L = LIVELY[this.who] ?? .8, t = now / 1000 + this.phase;
    const base = POSE[this.mood].map(v => v * L);
    // idle drift: slow, uneven, never repeating exactly
    const idle = [Math.sin(t * .7) * 2.2 + Math.sin(t * 1.3) * 1, Math.sin(t * .9) * 1.2, Math.sin(t * .5) * 1.6].map(v => v * L);
    const target = base.map((v, i) => v + idle[i] + this.kick[i]);
    if (this.talking) target[1] += Math.sin(t * 13) * 1.4 * L;               // nods with the words
    if (this.mood === 'laughing') target[1] -= Math.abs(Math.sin(t * 9)) * 2.5 * L;
    const k = 1 - Math.exp(-dt / 0.12);
    this.pose = this.pose.map((v, i) => v + (target[i] - v) * k);
    this.kick = this.kick.map(v => v * Math.exp(-dt / 0.18));
    const [yaw, pitch, roll] = this.pose;
    for (const [cls, d] of Object.entries(DEPTH)) {
      for (const el of this.g[cls]) {
        const tx = yaw * d, ty = pitch * d;
        // the features compress a little on the side turning away
        const sx = cls === 'L-feat' ? 1 - Math.abs(yaw) * 0.006 : 1;
        el.setAttribute('transform', cls === 'L-back'
          ? `rotate(${roll} 100 140) translate(${tx} ${ty})`
          : `translate(${tx} ${ty}) translate(100 101) scale(${sx} 1) translate(-100 -101)`);
      }
    }
    for (const el of this.head) el.setAttribute('transform', `rotate(${roll} 100 140)`);
    // blinks (ChildGBT almost never blinks)
    if (now > this.nextBlink && !['happy', 'laughing'].includes(this.mood)) {
      this.blinkUntil = now + 110;
      this.nextBlink = now + (this.who === 'childgbt' ? 6000 + Math.random() * 4000 : 2200 + Math.random() * 3200);
    }
    const shut = now < this.blinkUntil;
    for (const el of this.eyes) el.setAttribute('visibility', shut ? 'hidden' : 'visible');
    for (const el of this.shut) el.setAttribute('visibility', shut ? 'visible' : 'hidden');
    // mouth: alternate open and mood shape while talking
    if (this.talking && now > this.flap) this.flap = now + 90 + Math.random() * 70, this.open = !this.open;
    const open = this.talking && this.open;
    for (const el of this.mouth) el.setAttribute('visibility', open ? 'hidden' : 'visible');
    for (const el of this.talk) el.setAttribute('visibility', open ? 'visible' : 'hidden');
  }
}

// Rig every portrait in new markup; one loop drives them all.
function rigAll(root) {
  if (document.body.classList.contains('still') || matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches) return;
  for (const tile of root.querySelectorAll('.tile')) if (!tile.rig) new Rig(tile);
}
let rigLast = performance.now();
(function loop(now) {
  const dt = Math.min(0.05, (now - rigLast) / 1000); rigLast = now;
  for (const r of RIGS) { if (!r.tile.isConnected) RIGS.delete(r); else r.step(now, dt); }
  requestAnimationFrame(loop);
})(rigLast);

```

`design/mockups/ui/screens.js`:

```js
// Every screen at 1080p, built only from `ui`. Positions match the game (client/src/*.rs).
const shot = n => `${A}shots/${n}`;

// ---- menu frame: numbered list left, wordmark bottom left, you top right, page right ----
// The frame stays while pages swap inside #page and #extra (see go() in index.html).
const MENU_ITEMS = [['01', 'Play', 'プレイ', 'play'], ['02', 'Practice', '練習', 'practice'], ['03', 'Settings', '設定', 'settings'], ['04', 'Voice', '音声', 'voice'], ['05', 'Quit', '終了', '']];
function menuFrame(page, content, extra = '') {
  // depth: the space and the far 16 sit back, the list and the page float in front (parallax)
  return `<div class="space" data-tilt="none" data-depth="-0.6"></div><div class="far16" data-tilt="none" data-depth="-3">16</div>
  <div class="abs scan" style="inset:0"></div>
  <div class="abs tune" style="left:80px;top:200px;width:560px" data-tilt="y 16" data-hinge="left center" data-depth="0.3">${ui.nav(MENU_ITEMS.map(([n, l, j, k]) => [n, l, j, l === page, k]))}</div>
  <div class="abs jp tune" style="left:92px;bottom:262px;font-size:16px;color:var(--tx2);--i:3" data-tilt="y 12" data-hinge="left center">ブートレグ・シックスティーン</div>
  <div class="abs tune" style="left:88px;bottom:96px;display:flex;align-items:flex-end;gap:10px;--i:4" data-tilt="y 12" data-hinge="left center"><span class="display">Bootleg</span><span class="wm16"><span class="display">16</span></span></div>
  <div class="tune" style="--i:1" data-tilt="none">${ui.identity(80)}</div>
  <div id="page" class="abs tune plate${content ? '' : ' empty'}" style="left:680px;width:fit-content;min-width:640px;max-width:1180px;top:160px;--i:2" data-tilt="y -10" data-hinge="right center" data-depth="0.2">${content}</div><div id="extra" data-tilt="none">${extra}</div>`;
}

// Match found: over the menu, the blurred menu behind (like menus over the game).
function matchFound(accepted, you) {
  const slots = Array.from({ length: 10 }, (_, i) => `<i class="mf-slot${i < accepted ? ' on' : ''}${you && i === accepted - 1 ? ' you' : ''}" style="--i:${i}"></i>`).join('');
  return `<div class="mf tune" style="--i:0"><div class="mf-box">
    <div class="label" style="color:var(--amber)">Casual 5v5 · ready check</div>
    <div class="display mf-title">Match found</div>
    <div class="mf-slots">${slots}</div>
    <div class="label" style="margin-top:12px">${accepted} of 10 accepted</div>
    <div class="mf-timer"><i style="width:${you ? 46 : 72}%"></i></div>
    <div class="label mf-left">0:${you ? '09' : '14'}</div>
    <div style="margin-top:32px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;align-items:center;gap:12px">
      ${you ? ui.primary('Accepted', 'Waiting for ' + (10 - accepted), true).replace('class="primary off"', 'class="primary off mf-wait"') : ui.primary('Accept', 'Enter').replace('class="primary"', 'class="primary mf-accept"')}
      ${you ? '' : ui.chip('Decline')}
    </div></div></div>`;
}

// Under a player's scoreboard row (mouse freed with right-click): report, and for teammates a
// kick vote.
function playerMenu(name, mate) {
  return `<div class="tune" style="display:flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;height:56px;padding-left:120px">
    <span class="label" style="margin-right:8px">${name}</span>${['Cheating', 'Griefing', 'Abuse'].map(r => ui.chip('Report · ' + r)).join('')}
    ${mate ? '<span style="width:1px;height:28px;background:var(--line-2);margin:0 8px"></span>' + ui.chip('Vote to kick') : ''}</div>`;
}

// Menu pages draw inside the shared frame.
for (const s of Object.values(SCREENS)) if (s.menu) s.html = () => menuFrame(s.menu, s.page(), s.extra());

// ---- in game ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Every HUD panel: rounded, tinted to your team, an edge light on top in your team's colour
// (flares on events), and the same motion language as the menus (hud.js runs the live demo).
const MIC = `url('data:image/svg+xml,${encodeURIComponent('<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><rect x="8" y="2" width="8" height="13" rx="4"/><path d="M5 11a7 7 0 0 0 14 0" fill="none" stroke="#000" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round"/><path d="M12 18v4M8 22h8" stroke="#000" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round"/></svg>')}')`;
const hudIco = (n, w, h, c, extra = '') => `<i class="spr" style="--s:url(${A}hud/${n}.png);width:${w}px;height:${h}px;color:${c}"${extra}></i>`;
// One voice row: mic, live level, the name in its team's colour, the channel. Yours carries
// the amber bar on the outer (left) edge.
const voiceRow = (name, color, ch, you) => `<div class="vc panel hud tune${you ? ' you bar-l' : ''}" data-voice="${name}">
  <i class="spr vc-mic" style="--s:${MIC};width:18px;height:18px;color:${you ? 'var(--amber)' : color}"></i>
  <span class="vc-lv">${[6, 12, 9, 4].map(h => `<i style="--h:${h}px"></i>`).join('')}</span>
  <span class="vc-name" style="color:${you ? 'var(--tx1)' : color}">${name}</span><span class="label vc-ch">${ch}</span></div>`;
// A teammate's tag over their head: name (mic and live level when they talk), health under it,
// the pip pointing down at them. Far teammates fade (game: teammates.rs).
const mateTag = (x, y, name, hp, talking, fade = 1) => `<div class="abs mtag" style="left:${x}px;top:${y}px;opacity:${fade}">
  ${talking ? `<i class="spr" style="--s:${MIC};width:18px;height:18px;color:var(--ct-color);margin-bottom:2px"></i>` : ''}<div class="mt-name"><span>${name}</span></div>
  <div class="mt-hp"><i style="width:${hp}%;${hp <= 25 ? 'background:var(--bad)' : ''}"></i></div><i class="mt-pip"></i></div>`;

// Spectating (game: spectate.rs + hud): the same corners as playing, showing who you watch, and
// one plate at the bottom: who it is, their game this match, how to switch.
function spectate() {
  const corners = hud().replace(/<div class="abs keep"[\s\S]*?<\/div><\/div>\s*<\/div>/, '');
  // hidden while watching: the crosshair
  return `<style>.stage .xhair { display: none !important; }</style>${corners}
  ${mateTag(1180, 358, 'kova', 64, true)}${mateTag(1490, 410, 'vera', 18, false, .55)}
  <div class="abs spec tune" style="left:50%;bottom:var(--safe);transform:translateX(-50%)">
    <div class="label" style="color:var(--tx2)">Watching</div>
    <div class="sp-row"><span class="h3" style="color:var(--ct-color);text-transform:none">Ghost</span>
      <span class="sp-stat"><b>14</b> K</span><span class="sp-stat"><b>9</b> D</span><span class="sp-stat"><b>92</b> ADR</span></div>
    <div class="sp-keys"><span class="label"><b class="key">Mouse 1</b> Next</span><span class="label"><b class="key">Mouse 2</b> Previous</span></div>
  </div>`;
}

function hud() {
  const ticks = (c, n) => `<div style="display:flex;gap:4px">${[0, 1, 2, 3, 4].map(i => `<i style="width:28px;height:4px;border-radius:2px;background:${i < n ? c : 'var(--line-2)'}"></i>`).join('')}</div>`;

// Strays side. [name, price, art, ammo or note, damage, rpm, move speed, penetration]; equipment has no gun stats.
const BUY = [
  ['Pistols', [['Glock-18', 400, 'gun/glock18', '20 / 120', 25, 400, 250, 1], ['USP', 500, 'gun/usp', '12 / 100', 34, 352, 250, 1], ['Desert Eagle', 650, 'gun/deagle', '7 / 35', 54, 267, 250, 2]]],
  ['SMGs', [['MAC-10', 1400, 'gun/mac10', '30 / 100', 29, 857, 250, 1], ['MP5', 1500, 'gun/mp5navy', '30 / 120', 26, 750, 250, 1], ['UMP45', 1700, 'gun/ump45', '25 / 100', 30, 571, 250, 1], ['P90', 2350, 'gun/p90', '50 / 100', 26, 857, 245, 1]]],
  ['Rifles', [['Galil', 2000, 'gun/galil', '35 / 90', 30, 666, 240, 2], ['AK-47', 2500, 'gun/ak47', '30 / 90', 36, 600, 221, 2], ['Scout', 2750, 'gun/scout', '10 / 90', 75, 48, 260, 3], ['AWP', 4750, 'gun/awp', '10 / 30', 115, 41, 210, 3]]],
  ['Equipment', [['Kevlar', 650, 'hud/suit_full', 'Armor 100'], ['Kevlar + Helmet', 1000, 'hud/suithelmet_full', 'Armor 100 · helmet'], ['Flashbang', 200, 'gun/flashbang', 'Max 2'], ['HE Grenade', 300, 'gun/hegrenade', 'Max 1'], ['Smoke Grenade', 300, 'gun/smokegrenade', 'Max 1']]],
];
const FUNDS = 3250;
const buyState = { cat: 2, sel: 1 };

function buyCards(cat, sel) {
  return BUY[cat][1].map((g, i) => {
    const cant = g[1] > FUNDS, on = i === sel, icon = g[2].startsWith('hud/');
    const art = icon ? `<i class="spr abs" style="--s:url(${A}${g[2]}.png);left:50%;top:52px;width:88px;height:88px;margin-left:-44px;color:${cant ? 'var(--tx3)' : 'var(--tx1)'}"></i>`
      : `<i class="gun abs" style="--s:url(${A}${g[2]}.png);left:40px;right:40px;top:52px;height:88px;${cant ? 'filter:grayscale(1) brightness(.45)' : ''}"></i>`;
    return `<div class="card tune${on ? ' sel' : ''}" data-item="${i}" style="--i:${i};height:200px;padding:20px var(--pad);cursor:pointer">
      <div style="display:flex"><span class="label n">${String(i + 1).padStart(2, '0')}</span><span class="label" style="margin-left:auto">${g[3]}</span></div>${art}
      <div class="abs" style="left:var(--pad);right:var(--pad);bottom:18px;display:flex;align-items:baseline"><span class="h3" style="color:${cant ? 'var(--tx3)' : 'var(--tx1)'}">${g[0]}</span><span class="num-s" style="margin-left:auto;font-size:20px;color:${cant ? 'var(--bad)' : 'var(--tx1)'}">$${g[1]}</span></div></div>`;
  }).join('');
}

function buyDetails(cat, sel) {
  const g = BUY[cat][1][sel], cant = g[1] > FUNDS, icon = g[2].startsWith('hud/');
  const size = Math.min(96, Math.floor(404 / (g[0].length * 0.43)));
  const spec = g.length > 4
    ? [['Damage', g[4], g[4] / 120], ['Fire rate', `${g[5]} rpm`, g[5] / 900], ['Magazine', g[3], 0], ['Move speed', g[6], g[6] / 260], ['Penetration', g[7], g[7] / 3]]
    : [['Use', g[3], 0]];
  return `<div class="tune"><div class="label" style="color:var(--amber)">${BUY[cat][0]} · selected</div>
    <div class="display" style="font-size:${size}px;line-height:96px;height:96px;margin-top:12px;white-space:nowrap">${g[0]}</div></div>
    ${icon ? `<i class="spr tune" style="--s:url(${A}${g[2]}.png);display:block;width:120px;height:120px;margin:24px auto;color:var(--tx1);--i:1"></i>` : `<i class="gun tune" style="--s:url(${A}${g[2]}.png);height:120px;margin:24px 0;--i:1"></i>`}
    ${spec.map((s, i) => `<div class="tune" style="--i:${i + 2};display:grid;grid-template-columns:130px 1fr 112px;gap:16px;align-items:center;height:44px;border-top:1px solid var(--line)"><span class="label">${s[0]}</span><div class="meter"${s[2] ? '' : ' style="visibility:hidden"'}><i style="width:${Math.min(1, s[2]) * 100}%"></i></div><span class="num-s" style="text-align:right;font-size:16px">${s[1]}</span></div>`).join('')}
    <div class="abs" style="left:32px;right:32px;bottom:32px">${(cant ? ui.primary(`Buy · $${g[1]}`, `Need $${g[1] - FUNDS}`, true) : ui.primary(`Buy · $${g[1]}`)).replace('min-width', 'width')}</div>`;
}

function buy() {
  const { cat, sel } = buyState;
  return `<div class="abs tune" style="left:var(--margin);right:var(--margin);top:120px;height:96px;display:flex;align-items:flex-end;padding-bottom:var(--pad);border-bottom:1px solid var(--line)">
      <div><div class="label" style="color:var(--t-color)">Buy · Strays · 0:14 left</div><div class="ptitle"><div class="row"><span class="h2">Armory</span><span class="jp">武器庫</span></div></div></div>
      <div class="bteam"><div class="label">Team</div><div class="row">${[['kova', 4350], ['vera', 1200], ['rook', 800, 1]].map(([n, m, dead]) => `<div class="bt${m < 2700 ? ' low' : ''}${dead ? ' dead' : ''}"><span>${n}</span><b>$${m}</b></div>`).join('')}</div></div>
      <div style="margin-left:48px;text-align:right"><div class="label">Funds</div><div style="font:700 44px var(--f-num);margin-top:4px"><span style="color:var(--ok)">$</span>${FUNDS}</div></div></div>
    <div class="abs tune" style="left:var(--margin);top:240px;width:360px;--i:1">${ui.nav(BUY.map((c, i) => [String(i + 1).padStart(2, '0'), c[0], '', i === cat]), 'compact buycats')}

}

function scores() {
  const hist = ['ct:d_skull', 't:c4', 'ct:defuser', 'ct:d_skull', 't:d_skull', 'ct:stopwatch', 't:c4', 'ct:d_skull', 't:d_skull', 'ct:defuser', 'ct:d_skull', 't:d_skull', 'now'];
  const strip = Array.from({ length: 24 }, (_, i) => hist[i] || '').map(r => {
    if (!r || r === 'now') return `<div style="flex:1;height:40px;background:var(--bg1);box-shadow:inset 0 0 0 ${r ? '2px var(--amber)' : '1px var(--line)'}"></div>`;
    const [t, n] = r.split(':'), c = t === 'ct' ? 'var(--ct-color)' : 'var(--t-color)';
    return `<div style="flex:1;height:40px;background:var(--bg1);box-shadow:inset 0 calc(-1 * var(--bar)) 0 ${c};display:grid;place-items:center">${ui.ico(n, 26, 26, c)}</div>`;
  }).join('');
  const row = (r) => `<div style="display:grid;grid-template-columns:96px 1fr 96px 96px;align-items:center;height:48px;padding:0 var(--pad);border-top:1px solid var(--line);${r[4] ? 'background:var(--amber-wash);box-shadow:inset var(--bar) 0 0 var(--amber)' : ''};color:${r[3] === 'Dead' ? 'var(--tx3)' : 'var(--tx1)'}">
    <span>${r[3] ? ui.status(r[3], { C4: 'c4', Kit: 'kit', Dead: 'dead', Bot: '' }[r[3]]) : ''}</span><span class="body" style="font-size:19px">${r[0]}</span><span class="num-s" style="text-align:right">${r[1]}</span><span class="num-s" style="text-align:right">${r[2]}</span></div>${r[5] ? playerMenu(r[0], r[5] === 'mate') : ''}`;
  const team = (name, jp, score, c, rows, i) => `<div class="tune" style="--i:${i};margin-top:32px">
    <div style="display:flex;align-items:center;background:var(--bg1);box-shadow:inset var(--bar) 0 0 ${c}">
      <div style="padding:12px var(--pad);flex:1;display:flex;align-items:baseline;gap:var(--gap)"><span class="h2" style="font-size:40px">${name}</span><span class="jp">${jp}</span><span class="label">${rows.length} players</span></div>
      <div class="num-m" style="padding:0 var(--pad);color:${c}">${String(score).padStart(2, '0')}</div></div>
    <div style="display:grid;grid-template-columns:96px 1fr 96px 96px;height:36px;align-items:center;padding:0 var(--pad)"><span></span><span class="label">Player</span><span class="label" style="text-align:right">K</span><span class="label" style="text-align:right">D</span></div>
    ${rows.map(row).join('')}</div>`;
  return `<div class="abs" style="left:360px;right:360px;top:160px">
    <div class="tune" style="display:flex;align-items:center"><span class="label">de_dust · Round 13</span><span class="num-s" style="margin-left:auto">1:42</span></div>
    <div class="tune" style="display:flex;gap:4px;margin-top:20px;--i:1">${strip}</div>
    ${team('Bureau', 'ビューロー', 7, 'var(--ct-color)', [['anas', 18, 9, 'Kit', 1], ['Ghost', 15, 10, '', 0, 'mate'], ['Sarge', 9, 11], ['Hawk', 11, 12, 'Dead'], ['Nova', 6, 13, 'Bot']], 2)}
    ${team('Strays', 'ストレイズ', 5, 'var(--t-color)', [['Viper', 17, 11], ['Kane', 8, 12, 'C4'], ['Mako', 7, 13], ['Rook', 12, 13, 'Dead'], ['Blitz', 10, 12, 'Dead']], 3)}</div>`;
}

// Loading (game: status_screens.rs): the map, the steps, real progress, Esc to cancel.
const STEPS = ['Starting server', 'Contacting server', 'Loading map', 'Joining'];
function loading(step, progress) {
  const rows = STEPS.map((t, i) => `<div class="ld-step${i < step ? ' done' : ''}${i === step ? ' now' : ''}"><i></i><span>${t}</span></div>`).join('');
  return `<div class="abs ld tune">
    <div class="label">Practice · solo</div>
    <div class="display ld-map">de_dust2</div>
    <div class="ld-steps">${rows}</div>
    <div class="ld-bar"><i style="width:${progress * 100}%"></i></div>
    <div class="ld-pct">${Math.round(progress * 100)}%</div>
  </div>
  <div class="abs" style="left:var(--margin);bottom:48px"><span class="chip" style="gap:12px">Cancel <b class="key" style="margin:0">Esc</b></span></div>`;
}

// A notice (game: status_screens.rs, crate::notice::Notice): over the menu, blurred behind.
function notice(title, body, retry, info) {
  return `<div class="mf tune" style="--i:0"><div class="mf-box nt">
    <div class="label" style="color:${info ? 'var(--tx2)' : 'var(--bad)'}">${info ? 'Notice' : 'Error'}</div>
    <div class="display nt-title">${title}</div>
    <div class="nt-body">${body}</div>
    <div class="nt-actions">${retry ? ui.primary('Retry', 'Enter') : ui.primary('Back', 'Enter')}${retry ? `<span class="chip" style="gap:12px">Back <b class="key" style="margin:0">Esc</b></span>` : ''}</div>
  </div></div>`;
}

// The server went quiet mid-match (game: crate::game::Reconnecting).
function reconnecting(since, giveUp) {
  return `<div class="panel hud rc tune"><i class="edge" style="background:var(--bad)"></i>
    <div class="label" style="color:var(--bad)">Connection interrupted</div>
    <div class="rc-line">Reconnecting <b>${since} s</b></div>
    <div class="rc-bar"><i style="width:${(1 - since / giveUp) * 100}%"></i></div>
    <div class="label" style="color:var(--tx3)">Esc · leave match</div>
  </div>`;
}
```

`design/mockups/ui/tokens.css`:

```css
/* bootleg16 · Interference. Mirrors client/src/ui/tokens.rs name for name: change both together.
   The UI is a signal. At rest it is clean; when something changes it splits into its two
   channels (Bureau cyan, Strays pink) and tunes back in. Amber is you: your selection, your
   main action, your row. */
:root {
  color-scheme: dark;
  /* surfaces, darkest to lightest */
  --bg0: #07080B; --bg1: #0E1116; --bg2: #151A21; --bg3: #1D242D;
  --hud-bg: rgba(7, 9, 12, .76);
  /* text */
  --tx1: #EAF2F8; --tx2: #8E9BA8; --tx3: #56616D;
  /* you */
  --amber: #FFA000; --amber-ink: #170E00;
  --amber-wash: rgba(255, 160, 0, .08); --amber-wash-2: rgba(255, 160, 0, .16);
  /* the two channels = the two sides */
  --ch-a: #49C6FF; --ch-b: #FF4F8B;
  --ct-color: var(--ch-a); --t-color: var(--ch-b);
  /* states */
  --ok: #5BE3A0; --bad: #FF4040;
  /* lines */
  --line: rgba(200, 230, 255, .10); --line-2: rgba(200, 230, 255, .24); --line-3: rgba(200, 230, 255, .45);
  --backdrop: rgba(7, 8, 11, .72);

  /* space, 1080p px (the game scales with the window height) */
  --gap-xs: 4px; --gap-s: 8px; --gap: 16px; --pad: 24px; --safe: 32px; --margin: 96px;
```

```js
// Components as functions, one per function in client/src/ui/. Screens only call these.
const A = 'assets/';
// The four assistants: colour, channel, face sheet, and how their words arrive.
const AI = {
  claudette: { name: 'Claudette', c: '#E8875F', ch: '01', face: 'claudette', arrive: 'Streams word by word' },
  childgbt: { name: 'ChildGBT', c: '#6FE3C1', ch: '02', face: 'childgbt', arrive: 'Types each character, cursor blinking' },
  twins: { name: 'Twins', c: '#A98BFF', ch: '03', face: 'sister', arrive: 'Her line, then he cuts in' },
  grumpk: { name: 'Grumpk', c: '#D4FF3A', ch: '04', face: 'grumpk', arrive: 'Slams in all at once' },
};
// small tiles crop to the face so it reads at UI size
const TILE_VIEW = '44 42 112 112';
const MOODS = ['neutral', 'happy', 'laughing', 'smug', 'shocked', 'thinking', 'worried', 'sad', 'annoyed'];

const ui = {
  // A square portrait tile in the assistant's colour.
  portrait: (ai, size, mood = 'neutral', face = AI[ai].face) => `<div class="tile" style="--c:${AI[ai].c};width:${size}px;height:${size}px" data-face="${face}" data-mood="${mood}">${faceSvg(face, AI[ai].c, mood, false, size < 100 ? TILE_VIEW : undefined)}</div>`,
  // The uplink (in matches only, bottom centre): the icon centred in the top edge of a HUD
  // panel, waveforms out to both sides, the name and the line centred.
  // Twins: "her mood|his mood" and "her line|his line"; his line opens a second row.
  uplink: (ai, mood, text, { style = '' } = {}) => {
    const a = AI[ai], lines = text.split('|'), moods = mood.split('|');
    const wave = side => `<span class="ul-wave ${side}">${[14, 9, 16, 11, 8, 12, 6, 9, 4, 5].map((h, k) => `<i style="--k:${k};--h:${h}px"></i>`).join('')}</span>`;
    return `<div class="uplink talking" style="--c:${a.c};${style}" data-ai="${ai}" data-text="${text.replace(/"/g, '&quot;')}" data-moods="${mood}">
      <div class="ul-face">${ui.portrait(ai, 88, moods[0])}<i class="ul-lock"></i></div>
      <div class="ul-band"><i class="ul-edge"></i><i class="ul-sweep"></i><i class="ul-timer"></i>${wave('l')}${wave('r')}
        <div class="label ul-name">${a.name}${lines.length > 1 ? ' · him' : ''}</div>
        ${lines.map((l, i) => `<div class="ul-row${i ? ' two' : lines.length > 1 ? ' past' : ''}"><div class="ul-in"><div class="ul-line">${l}</div><i class="ul-scan l"></i><i class="ul-scan r"></i></div></div>`).join('')}
      </div></div>`;
  },
  t: (cls, s, color) => `<span class="${cls}"${color ? ` style="color:${color}"` : ''}>${s}</span>`,
  navItem: (num, label, jp, on, go) => `<div class="item${on ? ' on' : ''}"${go ? ` data-go="${go}"` : ''}><span class="label n">${num}</span><span class="h2">${label}</span>${jp ? `<span class="jp">${jp}</span>` : ''}</div>`,
  nav: (items, cls = '') => `<div class="nav ${cls}"><i class="ind"></i>${items.map(i => ui.navItem(...i)).join('')}</div>`,
  chip: (label, on, extra = '', style = '') => `<span class="chip${on ? ' on' : ''}"${style ? ` style="${style}"` : ''}>${extra}${label}</span>`,
  chips: (labels, on) => `<div class="chips">${labels.map(l => ui.chip(l, l === on)).join('')}</div>`,
  stepper: v => `<div class="stepper">${ui.chip('−')}<span class="v">${v}</span>${ui.chip('+')}</div>`,
  settingRow: (name, controls) => `<div class="srow"><span class="name">${name}</span><div class="chips" style="align-items:center">${controls}</div></div>`,
  primary: (label, hint = 'Enter', off = false) => `<div class="primary${off ? ' off' : ''}"><b>${label}</b><span class="label">${hint}</span></div>`,
  pageTitle: (eyebrow, title, jp) => `<div class="ptitle"><div class="label">${eyebrow}</div><div class="row"><span class="h2">${title}</span><span class="jp">${jp}</span></div></div>`,
  status: (s, kind = '') => `<span class="label status ${kind}">${s}</span>`,
  label: (s, mt = 32) => `<div class="label" style="margin:${mt}px 0 12px">${s}</div>`,
  avatar: (a, b, size = 44, presence) => `<div class="av" style="--a:${a};--b:${b};width:${size}px;height:${size}px">${presence ? `<i style="--p:${presence}"></i>` : ''}</div>`,
  // Who you are, top right.
  identity: (top, height) => `<div class="abs panel" style="right:var(--margin);top:${top}px;${height ? `height:${height}px;` : ''}display:flex;align-items:center;gap:var(--gap);padding:12px var(--pad) 12px 12px">
    ${ui.avatar('#c9733f', '#3b2418', 44, 'var(--ok)')}<div><div class="body" style="font-weight:700">anas_1412</div><div class="label">Online · via Steam</div></div></div>`,
  // Invite toast: right edge, so the amber bar is on the right.
  toast: (top) => `<div class="abs panel raised bar-r tune" style="right:var(--margin);top:${top}px;width:480px;padding:var(--gap) 20px;z-index:4">
    <div style="display:flex;gap:var(--gap);align-items:center">${ui.avatar('#5b8fd6', '#1b2a44')}<div><div class="label" style="color:var(--amber)">Party invite</div><div class="body"><b>kova</b> invited you to their party</div></div></div>

  vote: (what, yes, no, needed, total, left) => `<div class="vote tune">
    <div class="vote-head"><span class="label" style="color:var(--amber)">Vote</span><span class="h3" style="font-size:20px">${what}</span><span class="label" style="margin-left:auto">${left}</span></div>
    <div class="vote-bar">${Array.from({ length: total }, (_, i) => `<i class="${i < yes ? 'yes' : i >= total - no ? 'no' : ''}"></i>`).join('')}<b style="left:${needed / total * 100}%"></b></div>
    <div class="vote-keys"><span class="label"><b class="key">F1</b> Yes · ${yes}</span><span class="label">${needed} needed</span><span class="label">No · ${no} <b class="key">F2</b></span></div></div>`,
  // A round-level announcement in the centre (voted out, surrendered).
  announce: (title, sub, c) => `<div class="announce tune"${c ? ` style="--c:${c}"` : ''}><div class="h2">${title}</div><i></i><div class="an-sub">${sub}</div></div>`,
  ico: (n, w, h, c = 'var(--tx1)') => `<i class="spr" style="--s:url(${A}hud/${n}.png);width:${w}px;height:${h}px;color:${c}"></i>`,
};
```

`docs/Context.md`:

```md
# Context (engine session handoff)

Everything a new session needs to take over the **engine side** of bootleg16. Read it top to
bottom once.
- The HUD and screens side: `docs/ContextHUD.md`, owned by the UI session.
- Open items: `docs/TODO.md`.
- Lessons and traps: `docs/GOTCHAS.md`.
- Specs: `docs/WEAPONS.md`, `RULES.md`, `MOVEMENT.md`, `NETWORKING.md`, `MAPS.md`, `UI.md`.

## Start here

1. `git pull`, then `git log --oneline -15` to see the latest work.
2. Read the user's auto-memory index:
   `~/.claude/projects/-home-blackbox-bootleg16/memory/MEMORY.md`. It holds standing rules
   and preferences (short answers, no Claude co-author, Wayland only, art direction and more).
3. Check whether the UI session is up. It may be paused: run `ListAgents` and look for
   "Game HUD/UI design concepts".
4. **A decision is open with the user:** start the sound work (Next, item 1), or let the UI
   session do a release build first. Ask before starting if they haven't said.

## How the user works

- Short answers, scanned, not read. A few lines, no long sections.
- Decide game-dev questions yourself and proceed. The user is not a game-dev expert.
- "Do it" means implement, test, commit and push.
- Mid-task messages often add work. Note it, finish the current step, then do it.
- Before saying a change is done, check it on screen (see Testing).

## The project

A CS 1.6 remake in Rust and Bevy 0.20, multiplayer first, shipping on Steam (Windows and
Linux). For now it plays on the CS 1.6 files from the user's own install. It runs at
128 tick.

| Crate | What it does |
|---|---|
| `goldsrc` | Valve formats: BSP, WAD, MDL (with posing), SPR, TGA, decals |
| `sim` | Shared game code, run by both client and server: movement, collision, weapons, grenades, doors and buttons, breakables, zones, hitboxes, `anim` |
| `net` | Protocol (now **v31**), client, server, delta snapshots, crypto, lobby protocol, bots, demos, reports |
| `server` | Dedicated server binary, plus the report review tool (`--reports`, `--review N`) |
| `client` | The game. One plugin per concern, `main.rs` only registers them |
| `lobby` | Matchmaking: parties, the casual queue, custom games |

## Rules that always hold

- Build with `systemd-run --user --scope -q -p MemoryMax=3G -- cargo build -p <crate> -j 2`.
  An uncapped build froze the PC.
- Don't change Cargo features or profiles: that rebuilds Bevy, which takes 30-45 min.
- Run only the tests for what changed.
- Wayland only: run the client with `env -u DISPLAY`.
- No god files. One module and plugin per concern; split a file past about 400 lines.
- Commits: no Claude co-author or attribution trailer. This overrides the harness default.
- Never `git commit -a`: two sessions share one working tree. Add your own files by name.
- Game copy has no em dashes: grep for them before showing anything.
- Everyone has the same hitbox, height, eye and speed. Characters are cosmetic.
- The AI assistant only knows what the player knows. Every new piece of information the
  player can see gets an assistant trigger and lines (`client/src/assistant/`).
- `gamedata/` is tracked and still holds Valve's files (maps, radar images, texture packs) and an add-on of unknown origin: the repo must stay PRIVATE until they are replaced (docs/TODO.md). `dist/` is only build output (installers, bundles), git-ignored.
- Map pool: de_dust2, de_inferno, de_mirage (on hold), de_train. Keep Nuke.
- Every fix must work on both Windows and Linux.

## How fidelity is checked

- Facts come from ReGameDLL (GPL, used for facts only, never code) and from disassembling
  CS's `client.so` with `objdump`. It has DWARF symbols.
  - `EV_Fire*`: sound attenuations.
  - `EV_HLDM_PlayTextureSound` and `GunshotDecalTrace`: impact sounds and decals.
  - `CGameStudioModelRenderer`: how player models are posed and lit.
- Lighting:
  - The lightmap goes through `lightgammatable` (brightness 1, gamma 2.5).
  - Textures get `texgamma` (x^(2.0/2.5)).
  - Models are lit by `studio.wesl`: ambient plus shade, with the sun from `light_environment`.
- Additive sprites are uploaded as `Rgba8Unorm`, because GoldSrc adds them in display space.
  Each frame is placed by its origin.
- Assets come from one game data folder (`net::gamefiles`): `data/` next to the executable, in the repo `gamedata/` (tracked; the repo is private), or `BOOTLEG16_DIR`. It has `maps/`, `overviews/`, `models/`, `sound/`, `sprites/`, `gfx/` and the `.wad` files. Nothing is read from a Half-Life or CS install any more.

## Main systems and where they live

- **Netcode** (`net/src/client.rs`, `net/src/server/`):
  - Client prediction; snapshots are deltas against the last snapshot the client acked.
  - Lag compensation rewinds animated hitboxes; `sim::anim` is stepped by the server every
    tick.
  - Reliable events; encrypted seats for official servers.
  - The server drops a silent player after 5 s (`TIMEOUT_TICKS`).
- **Getting into a match** (`client/src/menu/connect.rs`, `loading.rs`, `notice.rs`):
  1. The steps are Starting server, Contacting server, Loading map and Joining, each slow
     one on its own thread (`loading::Job`).
  2. The map is parsed once and shared as `MapData`. Its `world` goes to the client and its
     `geometry` to `level.rs`. Other modules read `MapData.bsp` instead of loading the file
     again.
  3. The loading screen stays up into `InGame` until the first snapshot is in and the render
     world's pipeline queue has been empty for 5 frames (at most 15 s): `loading::reveal`.
  4. Every way back to the menu is a `Notice` (title, body, Retry when retrying can work).
- **Connection lost** (`game.rs`, `connection`):
  - After 3 s of server silence, `Reconnecting` appears and `Client::rejoin` says hello
    again, keeping the seat.
  - After 30 s it gives up with a notice.
  - Test: `net/tests/leavers.rs`, `a_dropped_player_rejoins_their_seat`.
- **Buying** (`net/src/server/buy.rs`):
  - Undo buys sells back this round's purchases while you can still buy, as CS2 does
    (`Client::undo_buys`).
- **Visuals**:
  - Decals and impacts (`impacts.rs`), sprites and glows (`glows.rs`), `explosions.rs`,
    `gibs.rs`.
  - Lit studio models (`studio.rs`); map sounds (`map_sounds.rs`).
  - Own bullet holes are predicted instantly (`ShotAssets` in `game.rs`).
- **Spectating** (`spectate.rs`):
  - While teammates are alive you watch in first person.
  - When your whole team is dead, the camera follows the last teammate who died in third
    person.
  - The crosshair is hidden while spectating.
- **Voice** (`client/src/voice/`):
  - Team voice is always on; proximity voice is for the living only.
  - Per-player mute and volume from the scoreboard; open mic with a noise gate.
  - Walls muffle proximity voice.

## Testing in the game

- Build `client`, then run `env -u DISPLAY target/debug/client de_dust2 --practice 0`.
  Join a server with `--connect host:port`.
- Screenshot hooks (environment variables):

| Variable | What it does |
|---|---|
| `BOOTLEG16_SCREENSHOT=path.png` | Save one frame, then quit |
| `BOOTLEG16_SCREENSHOT_AT` | Seconds before the frame is taken |
| `_LOOK=yaw,pitch` | Aim the camera |
| `_TEAM` | Join a team |
| `_SPECTATE` | Spectate |
| `_CAM=x,y,z` | Park the camera at a point |
| `BOOTLEG16_FIRE` | Hold fire |
| `BOOTLEG16_MENU_PAGE` | Open a menu page: `practice`, `join`, `settings`, `crosshair`, `assistant`, `keys`, `voice`, `characters`, `maps` |
| `BOOTLEG16_FAKE_PING` / `_LOSS` | Fake network conditions |

- Put screenshots in the session scratchpad and look at them before saying a change is done.
- Net tests (`net/tests/`) run a real server and clients over localhost and skip themselves
  when de_dust2 isn't installed. `common::Game` drives them; `simulate_network(0, 1.0)` cuts
  a client off.
- Killing processes: `pkill -f` once killed its own shell. Use `ps` and `kill <pid>`.

## Two sessions on one repo

- **Engine session (you):**
  - Netcode, sim, server and the lobby.
  - Loading, notice and reconnect logic.
  - Sound, rendering, models, players, effects, the view model and map sounds.
- **UI session ("Game HUD/UI design concepts"):**
  - Menu pages, the HUD, the buy menu, spectating screens, teammate tags.
  - `status_screens.rs`, `design/mockups`, the `ui/` design system.
- Message it with `SendMessage` (find it with `ListAgents`) before touching its files.
- For a shared interface, you write the logic and its resources, it draws the view. Commit
  both halves together, so the build never sees one without the other.
- `docs/TODO.md` is shared: pull before editing it.
- The UI session is **paused** by the user, and does the release build (`tools/bundle.sh`)
  only when the user says so. Its `docs/ContextHUD.md` was uncommitted at handoff: leave it
  to that session.

## Next (all in `docs/TODO.md`)

### 1. Sound system: one mixer

Today four separate paths play audio:

| Path | File | How it plays |
|---|---|---|
| Game sounds | `client/src/sound.rs` | A `Cue` enum; `play_cues` works out the gain once, at spawn, from `ear = w.client.me().eye()` and GoldSrc falloff |
| Map sounds | `map_sounds.rs` | Its own `gain()`, `one_shot` and `spawn_loop` (the falloff is written a second time) |
| UI tones | `ui/sound.rs` | Synthesized tones |
| Voice | `voice/` | Its own output stream |

All of them use `settings.volume` directly. Build:
- **One play function**, used by every path.
- **Volume buses**, each with a Settings slider: master, effects, ambience, UI, assistant,
  voice.
- **GoldSrc channels** per entity (weapon, body, voice, item, static): a new sound on a
  channel stops the one before it. Today a reload keeps playing after you switch weapons.
- **A voice cap**: limit how many sounds play at once and drop the quietest or oldest.
- **The camera as the listener.** `SpatialListener` is on the camera, but loudness is worked
  out from your own body, so spectating sounds wrong.
- **Live volume**: volume changes must reach sounds that are already playing.
- **Room reverb** from the maps' `env_sound` areas (`roomtype`), the way CS 1.6 changes the
  echo per area. Unverified: check the maps for these entities before building on it.

### 2. Weapon switch shows a character model for a moment

- Hypothesis, NOT verified, in `client/src/viewmodel.rs`, `update`:
  1. On a switch it spawns the new skinned parts with `spawn_skinned`, then calls
     `set_pose` on joints that don't exist until the commands are applied.
  2. So the first frame draws the bind or reference pose.
- If confirmed, fix: spawn the parts hidden, and show them once a pose has been applied.

### 3. Smoke cloud far too see-through

- `client/src/smoke.rs` draws 30 puffs of size 110, with puff alpha `0.9 x` a soft texture
  that falls off to the edge.
- CS uses gas puff sprites and is near-opaque in the middle.
- Make the core opaque. Check it from inside and outside the cloud.

### 4. Footsteps may use the wrong sound

- Reported in play, not confirmed.
- The file-number mapping already matches CS.
- Check the surface lookup in `sound.rs`, `Cue::Footstep`: it traces from the feet to 64
  units below. Unverified whether CS does the same: compare against the disassembly.
- Also check `step_set` and the materials map against CS for each map surface.

### 5. Not yet seen on screen

- The round timer's ticks.
- The full 30 s give-up of reconnecting.

### 6. Possible first-use hitches

- Effects drawn for the first time (explosions, gibs, glass) may compile shaders mid-game.
  Not confirmed.
- If it happens, warm them up behind the loading cover.
```

`docs/GOTCHAS.md`:

```md
# Gotchas and lessons learned

Things that cost time once. Read before touching the area; add to it when
something surprises you.

## Building on this machine

- **Cap every build**: `systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=3G -p MemorySwapMax=1G -- cargo build -j 2`.
  `.cargo/config.toml` sets `jobs = 2`. An uncapped Bevy build ran 8 rustc
  processes (~7 GB) and froze the desktop. First Bevy build ~15 min, rebuilds ~1 min.
- Automated screenshot runs open real windows on the user's desktop. They must
  ignore mouse and keyboard (`BOOTLEG16_SCREENSHOT` does that), or the user's
  clicks fire weapons in the test window.
- Time screenshots in seconds (`BOOTLEG16_SCREENSHOT_AT`), not frames: the frame
  rate varies a lot, so "frame 900" was sometimes only 3 s.

## Reverse engineering CS 1.6

- `cstrike/dlls/cs.so` (32-bit) has **full DWARF debug info** (types, enums, struct
  offsets). `cs_amd64.so` has none. Use `gdb -batch -ex 'ptype ...' cs.so` and
  `objdump -d -l -C` (the `-l` line info recovers the **source order** of code
  blocks that the compiler reordered: e.g. the 4 KickBack sets).
- Constants hide as: enums (prices), static tables (`weaponInfo`), immediates
  in `movl $0x...` (floats), `fld 0xADDR` (rodata floats/doubles), and integer
  division "magic numbers" (`0x51eb851f` + `sar 6` = `/200`).
- ReGameDLL_CS is a useful cross-check but **GPL**: read it for facts only, never
  copy code. Its `#ifdef REGAMEDLL_ADD/FIXES` branches change behaviour; the
  original is the `#else` branch. When it disagrees with the binary, the binary wins.
- Client-side cvars (e.g. `cl_movespeedkey 0.52`) live in `cl_dlls/client.so`
  as string pairs; engine cvars (`sv_*`) in `engine_i486.so`/`hw.so`. CS also
  forces some every round (`sv_accelerate 5`, `sv_friction 4`, `sv_stopspeed 75`).

## GoldSrc formats

- BSP texture names in the miptex lump have junk after the NUL: cut at the first NUL.
- Spawn points float above the floor (players drop onto it). Don't assume
  `origin.z - 36` is the floor; trace down first.
- Two kinds of BSP trees: clip hulls 1-3 (player-sized, for movement) and hull 0
  (exact geometry, render nodes + leaf contents: bullets, water, sky). A test
  world must give *both* a root, or line traces silently miss everything.
- GoldSrc traces that **start inside solid report fraction 0**. Bullet
  penetration relies on this (a bullet restarted inside a thick wall is stopped).
- MDL sequence header: `numblends` at +120, `animindex` at +124 (not +116/+120).
- CS player models have **9 aim blend sets** (pitch); level aim is the middle one.
  The rifle aim pose leans the head ~12 units forward: hitbox tests must use the
  posed positions, not "straight ahead at head height".
- `v_` view models are stored **left-handed**; CS 1.6 mirrors them (`cl_righthand 1`).
  Mirroring flips triangle winding, so swap two indices per triangle.
- `p_` weapon models have no animation of their own: pose them from the player's
  skeleton by bone name (`Model::borrow_pose`).
- `p_` models have extra bones the player lacks (`flash`, `Line02`, carrying the
  gun's vertices). Merge like GoldSrc: borrow matching bones, rebuild unmatched
  ones as `borrowed parent x own local`, never leave them at their rest pose.
- Each weapon has its own player body animation set (`ref_aim_ak47`, `_carbine`,
  `_rifle`, `_mp5`, `_onehanded`, ...): pose the body for the weapon in hand.
- Seen from the front, a rifle pointing at the camera looks like a vertical stick.
  Measure model extents before "fixing" orientation.
- `materials.txt` compares the first 12 characters of a texture name; a short
  listed name does *not* match a longer texture name.

## Coordinates and rendering (Bevy 0.20)

- GoldSrc is Z-up: `(x, y, z) -> (x, z, -y)` in Bevy. Yaw about Z equals the same
  angle about Bevy's Y. GoldSrc faces are clockwise: reverse winding.
- GoldSrc pitch is positive looking **down**; Bevy's is positive looking up.
- **Meshes must keep their CPU data** (`RenderAssetUsages::default()`). With
  `RENDER_WORLD` only, Bevy can't compute bounds, falls back to a box at the
  origin, and frustum-culls the whole map whenever the origin is off screen.
- Lightmaps: upload as linear `Rgba8Unorm` (not sRGB), `lightmap_exposure` 2.0,
  camera `Exposure { ev100: -log2(1.2) }` for exposure 1.0, `Tonemapping::None`.
- Bevy 0.20 API changes vs older docs: shaders are WESL; `FontSize::Px(..)`;
  `CursorOptions` is its own component; `MessageWriter<AppExit>`;
  `Assets::get_mut` returns a guard (`if let Some(mut m) = ...`); built-in
  `Lightmap` component with `UV_1`.
- Translucent effects seen from inside (smoke) need `cull_mode: None`.
- Audio: rodio's spatial sink scales loudness by 1/distance^2 (capped at 1). Shrink
  `SpatialScale` (1/4096) so it only pans, and apply GoldSrc falloff
  (`1 - dist * attn / 1000`) yourself. WAV needs Bevy's `wav` feature.
- Reload/draw/pin sounds are **animation events** (id 5004, file name in options)
  inside the `v_` models; event 5001 is the muzzle flash. Play them as frames pass.
- Glock: `shoot3` is the single-shot animation, `shoot`/`shoot2` are burst ones.
- A spectator/chase camera must trace to its spot and stop short of walls.

## Simulation and netcode

- CS clamps your input to the weapon's max speed **before** the crouch/walk
  multipliers (knife crouch-walk is 83 u/s, not 133).
- Jump stamina slows landing speed hard for ~1.3 s; a path that jumps often is
  much slower than 250 u/s. Not a bug.
- Weapon timers run on each player's **command clock** (`input number x tick`), not
  server time, so the client can replay its own shooting exactly.
- Accuracy uses **integer** division (`shots^3 / 200`): it is a step function.
- Recoil caps are reached right after each shot and then decay between shots;
  measure the peak, not a random moment.
- Lag compensation must rewind through **snapshot ticks only** (what clients
  actually blend between), or there's a ~0.6 unit error even on LAN.
- `HashMap` iteration order on the server is random: never rely on client order.
- After bumping `PROTOCOL_VERSION`, rebuild **all** binaries (client, server,
  examples). A stale server rejects new clients, which then just sit "connecting".
- Reload is ignored until the current fire cycle (`next_primary`) has passed.

## Tests

- Write the assertion from CS behaviour, then check the test itself when it
  fails: several "bugs" were wrong expectations (zoom lockout, shotgun cycle
  count, spawn heights, flash going off behind the victim).
- Prefer path length over displacement when checking that a player moved (walls).

## Client structure / UI (2026-10-15)
- Bevy 0.20: `BorderRadius` is a field of `Node` (`border_radius`), not a component.
- An `OnEnter` system that fails and sets `NextState` still lets that frame's `Update` run in the old state:
  in-game sets also need `run_if(resource_exists::<Walker>)` or they panic on the missing resource.
- Player models: GoldSrc draws legs from the gait sequence and the rest from the upper-body one,
  split at the first "Bip01 Spine" bone, in *local* bone space (`Model::player_pose`); mixing model-space
  matrices detaches the torso.
- Player aim blend: 0.5 + pitch/180 with GoldSrc pitch (down positive) — checked: -60 points the gun up.
- Death events arrive before the interpolated snapshot shows the player dead (4 ticks later):
  keep a "dying" set or the live model is redrawn on top of the corpse.

## Performance (2026-10-15)
- Server input queue: the speed-hack budget only allows real time, so a burst of inputs after a client
  hitch (map load) became a permanent backlog = ~120 ms of fake ping. Backlogs that last 1/4 s are dropped.
- KDE Wayland: `PresentMode::AutoNoVsync` still ran at 60; `Mailbox` runs free without tearing.
  FPS readings also drop to 60 whenever KWin throttles an unfocused/occluded test window — don't trust those.
- `Model::posed_mesh` used to decode every texture to RGBA per call (just for UV sizes): huge per-frame cost.
- Animating by rebuilding meshes re-uploads them every frame (`allocate_and_free_meshes` was the top render
  system). Players are GPU-skinned now: vertices in bone space (`Model::bind_mesh`), identity inverse binds,
  one joint entity per bone; bounds come from the bind pose, so skinned parts get `NoFrustumCulling`.
- `ClusterConfig::None` breaks Bevy 0.20 GPU clustering (zero-size texture errors); use `Single`.
- Profiling: `cargo build -p client --features profile` (bevy trace_chrome) into `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target-prof`
  (a full separate Bevy build, ~45 min at -j 2); the trace JSON is ~1 GB for 10 s. gdb can't attach to a running
  process (ptrace_scope 1): run it under gdb instead.
- Dev profile now builds our crates at opt-level 3 too (opt 1 cost a lot of fps); rebuilds ~3 min.

## Rounds (2026-10-16)
- Client snapshot state lags the server by a few ticks: tests that check "frozen during freeze time" must use
  the server's phase (`Server::round_phase`), not the client's, or they run into the next phase.
- Engine tests (movement, guns) now need a permissive `MatchConfig` (no freeze, money, friendly fire) or
  freeze time and buy zones get in the way: `tests/common::setup` does that; `setup_with` takes real rules.
- Child modules (`server/round.rs` etc.) can use the parent's private fields, but `fn`s in their `impl Server`
  blocks must be `pub(super)` for `server/mod.rs` to call them.
- `info_map_parameters bombradius` (de_nuke 350): C4 damage = radius, reach = 3.5 × radius, through walls.
- Head height: in the CS models the head centre is ~+19 over the origin, i.e. at eye level (+17), and leans
  forward of the origin by 1-12 units depending on the weapon pose. Shooting someone's back at eye level can
  hit the upper chest first. Hitboxes are posed per weapon (`Target::weapon`).
- Dev builds link Bevy dynamically, and the rpath is `$ORIGIN/`, but `libbevy_dylib-*.so` sits in
  `target/debug/deps/`. Running `target/debug/client` directly fails ("cannot open shared object file");
  use `cargo run` or `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=target/debug/deps:$(rustc --print sysroot)/lib`.
- After a protocol bump, rebuild the server too: an old `target/debug/server` refuses a new client
  ("server runs protocol N, you have N+1").
- Bevy `FromWorld` is blanket-implemented for `Default` types: don't derive `Default` on a resource that
  has its own `impl FromWorld`.

## Polish batch (2026-10-16)
- GoldSrc sky faces (gl_warp.c): rt +X, lf -X, bk +Y, ft -Y, up +Z, dn -Z; sides have s to the right, t up
  (as seen from inside). Bevy samples cubemaps in the WebGPU layout with world directions, so faces can't
  just be stacked: `sky.rs` resamples every cubemap texel by direction. Sky file names differ in case
  ("Des" -> "Desbk.tga"): look them up case-insensitively.
- CS 1.6 tagging is per *server frame* (+0.01 to the modifier and velocity × modifier each frame); HLDS ran
  ~100 fps, so `player::tagging` scales it to 1/100 s steps.
- Helper binaries (net/examples/*) go stale silently after a protocol bump: rebuild them or they're rejected.
- dust2's bomb-site crates are `func_breakable` with spawnflag 1 (only trigger), fired by the site's `target`.
- Bevy UI draws an `ImageNode` inside the node's padding (content box only). For a shaped
  background (the notched amber button), put the image on a box without padding and the
  padded content in a child.
- `add_plugins((...))` takes at most 15 plugins per tuple; nest a second tuple for more.
- A tight `LineHeight` (e.g. 0.8) clips tall display glyphs at the top; give the box some
  vertical padding instead of relying on the line box.

## Security (2026-10-16 review)
- Never make secrets (tickets, sessions, codes, cookies) with a seeded PRNG: xorshift64* output
  reveals its state, so one ticket gives away everyone's. Use `net::secure::random()` (OS).
- Every reply to an unauthenticated packet must be no bigger than the request (padding);
  `answers_never_outgrow_requests` checks the lobby's worst case. Cap lists in answers.
- Rate-limit tables must not let made-up addresses crowd out real players: players and
  strangers have separate tables, and the lobby's bookings bypass the stranger budget.
- Official servers take booked players only; an unreserved official server is not open.
- Tests run every bot/player from 127.0.0.1: per-IP limits must scale per player (or exempt
  loopback), or the tests fail in ways that look like game bugs.
- Never build a "keyed hash" from an invertible mixer (splitmix, xorshift): one output gives
  the key back. MACs and cookies use BLAKE3 keyed hashing (`net::secure::Cookies`).
- Timing-sensitive network tests can flake when every suite runs at once (CPU starved): give
  them generous game-time limits, and re-run alone before treating a failure as a bug.
- Bevy UI: a bundle can't hold the same component twice. `Icons::node` and `kit_text` already
  bring their `Node` / text parts: tweak them after spawning (`.entry::<Node>().and_modify`),
  don't add a second `Node` in the tuple (it panics at spawn, not at compile time).
- A Bevy system takes at most 16 parameters: split a big animation into systems that share
  their state through a component (the uplink: `animate` works out the timeline, `light` and
  `reveal` draw from it), instead of tuples of queries.
- A part that animates its own colour (a burst, a roll) fights any system that also sets that
  colour every frame: the setter skips while an `Anim` is on it (`Has<Anim>`).
- Nested animations share one `Base` (a node's colours before an animation) per node. Two
  races left menu rows blank until clicked again (the page tunes in while each row does): the
  first animation to finish restored and dropped the Base while the other still ran, and a
  second animation reaching a node in the same frame read the colours the first had just faded
  (the Base insert lands at the end of the frame). `anim` now restores a node only when the
  last animation covering it ends, and reuses Bases made earlier in the same frame. A blank
  screen that shows only the chips (their hover fades rewrite them) is this kind of bug.
- Sample a screen several times before trusting it: bugs that depend on frame timing show up
  in some captures only.

## NVIDIA + Wayland: fullscreen or resize kills the game
`wp_linux_drm_syncobj_surface_v1: error 3: explicit sync is used, but no buffer is attached`, then "Couldn't get swap chain texture: Lost". NVIDIA driver 615 on KDE Wayland, only on the NVIDIA GPU (Intel/Mesa is fine; `WGPU_ADAPTER_NAME=Intel` to compare). `main` sets `__NV_DISABLE_EXPLICIT_SYNC=1` before Vulkan starts. If it comes back on another driver, test with that variable first.

## Rendering the UI into an image and showing it on a surface breaks picking when the image is resized
The old 3D menu did this; after a resize hovers and clicks stopped working (layout and hit boxes no longer matched the drawn page). Keep menus on the window's own UI camera.

## Fullscreen took KDE down on the hybrid laptop (2026-10-18)
Journal (`journalctl -b 0`): after the game went fullscreen, `kwin_wayland_wrapper: intel: the execbuf ioctl keeps returning ENOMEM`, then `kwin_wayland` died with SIGABRT and the session restarted (looks like the PC crashed). Earlier, `NVRM: dmaAllocMapping_GM107: can't alloc VA space ... NV_ERR_NO_MEMORY`. Machine: Intel UHD drives the screen (KWin), the GTX 1650 renders (PRIME), NVIDIA 615.78, Mesa 26.2.4. The game itself is small (about 480 MiB VRAM, 875 MB RSS in the menu), so it is the buffer sharing between the two GPUs, not a leak of ours. Windowed has never crashed. So the game no longer uses the compositor's fullscreen: Settings has Window size and Borderless (an undecorated window the size of the screen, which is how most games do it), default is a 1920x1080 window. Do not test borderless on this machine without the user asking. Ideas to try later: run on the Intel GPU for the display test (`WGPU_ADAPTER_NAME=Intel`), `__NV_PRIME_RENDER_OFFLOAD=1`, a newer NVIDIA driver or KWin.

```

```md
# Maps

Four competitive maps in the bootleg16 world (Bureau vs Strays). Each takes the
structure of a classic layout, so players' knowledge transfers. The setting,
story, geometry, textures, props and names are new. Valve map names stay out of
the game and code.

Map names are working names for now; final names are chosen later.

## Story
In the 2040s, governments have outsourced policing, energy and transport to the
**Bureau**, a private security conglomerate. Rent, debt and power bills have
locked a generation out.
- **Strays:** a leaderless network of young people who believe the system can't
  be reformed, only broken. They bomb the places that keep it running.
  Motto: *"Nothing left to lose."*
- **Bureau:** the system is the only thing between people and chaos, and Strays
  attacks hurt ordinary people first. Motto: *"Order is mercy."*

Strays plant, Bureau defends. Each map's two bomb sites are fictional
Bureau-owned targets inside a real place.

**Neither side is simply right.** Loading screens and voice lines show the cost
on both sides. Each character has a personal reason for being on their side. The
movement is fictional, not a real party or protest group.

## The four maps
| Map | Pillar | Real place (look only) | Layout from |
|---|---|---|---|
| **port** | Supply | Container port, Rotterdam | Train |
| **data_center** | Surveillance | Server farm, Iceland | Dust2 |
| **bank** | Money | Financial district, Canary Wharf, London | Mirage |
| **high_rise** | Housing | Luxury tower under construction, Kowloon, Hong Kong | Inferno |

### Why each layout fits
- **port ← Train:**
  - Train is parallel rows of train cars as cover, with lanes between them; container stacks in rows are the same structure.
  - Train's upper routes (Ivy, the overpass) become the crane gantries.
- **data_center ← Dust2:**
  - Long A is the main server aisle;
  - short/catwalk is a raised-floor walkway;
  - mid with its doors is a central corridor with security doors;
  - B tunnels are the cable crawlspace under the floor.
- **bank ← Mirage:**
  - Mirage's A site is an open plaza watched from ramp, palace, connector and stairs. The bank atrium has the same angles from a mezzanine and glass bridges.
  - Mid with its window is the trading floor behind glass.
  - The B apartments are office corridors leading to the vault.
- **high_rise ← Inferno:**
  - Inferno is tight and on two levels: apartments, balconies over the lanes, stairs everywhere, one narrow choke (banana). The unfinished tower has the same: bare flats, open balconies, stairwells.
  - Banana is the narrow scaffolding run.

**Only the structure is copied.** Light, weather, textures, colours and
architecture come from the real place, never from the original map.

## Rules for every map
- **Layout:**
  - same lanes, sites, chokes and rotation times as the base layout (±5 %);
  - callouts are adapted to the setting.
- **Readability first:**
  - plain mid-value walls;
  - player silhouettes must pop against everything;
  - no busy textures at head height;
  - bomb sites marked with a large painted letter plus a site-colored light.
- **Factions:** Bureau defends, Strays attack. Spawns are styled to match: Bureau vans and barriers vs Strays bikes and graffiti.
- **One hero landmark per map,** visible from spawn:
  - port: the container cranes;
  - data_center: the steam from the cooling towers;
  - bank: the glass atrium;
  - high_rise: the tower crane.

## Status
**Not started.** We play on the CS 1.6 maps until the game itself is finished.
This is the plan for after that.

## Build plan (same structure, new build)
1. **Measure:** a tool reads the base BSP and records numbers only:
   - floor plan, floor/ceiling heights;
   - door and corridor widths, site zones, spawns.

   No Valve geometry or textures carry over.
2. **Greybox:** a generator rebuilds the structure from our own modular blocks.
   - It writes a TrenchBroom `.map`, which VHLT compiles to BSP v30.
   - The existing `goldsrc` loader, collision hulls and `sim` movement work unchanged.
3. **Verify** against the base, each within ±5 %:
   - walk times spawn → each site;
   - main sightline lengths;
   - door widths.
4. **Art pass:**
   - a modular kit per map, CC0 PBR textures overriding WAD textures by name, glTF props;
   - renderer upgrade: fog, bloom, colour grading.
   - Landmark pieces come from an artist or an asset store (CC0/Fab).
5. **Hand polish** in TrenchBroom, which opens the same `.map`.

**Tools needed then:** VHLT (build from source), plus TrenchBroom and Blender for hand work. None are installed yet.

**Mirage base:** not in the stock 1.6 install. The 1.6 community `de_mirage` (by BubkeZ, 2010) was installed 2026-10-16 from the user's download and loads in the client.

**Order:** data_center (Dust2 is our test map) → high_rise → port → bank.
```

```md
# Player movement (CS 1.6)

Code: `sim/src/pmove.rs` (movement), `sim/src/collision.rs` (hull traces).
Engine-free and deterministic: same inputs give the same result, so the server
and client can run it identically. It runs at 128 ticks/s (64 also works).

## Constants and where they come from

| Value | Number | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Gravity | 800 | engine cvar default (`hw.so`/`engine_i486.so`) |
| Accelerate | 5 | CS forces it every round: `cs.so` `RestartRound @ab424` |
| Friction | 4 | same, `@ab439` |
| Stop speed | 75 | same, `@ab44e` |
| Air accelerate | 10 | engine cvar default |
| Edge friction | 2 | engine cvar default |
| Step size | 18 | engine cvar default |
| Max velocity | 2000 | engine cvar default |
| Jump speed | 268.328 (45-unit jump) | `cs.so` `PM_Jump @1274bc` |
| Jump stamina | 1315.79, drains 1000/s | `PM_Jump @1274fc` |
| Stamina slowdown | `(100 − stamina × 0.019) / 100` on jump height and landing speed | `PM_Jump`, `PM_WalkMove` |
| Bunny-hop cap | over 1.2 × max speed → scaled to 0.8 of the cap | `PM_PreventMegaBunnyJumping` |
| Crouch speed | × 0.333 | `PM_Duck` |
| Air wish-speed cap | 30 | `PM_AirAccelerate` |
| Walkable floor | normal z ≥ 0.7 | `PM_CatagorizePosition`, `PM_WalkMove` |
| Standing / crouched box | 32×32×72 / 32×32×36 | map collision hulls 1 and 3 |
| Eye height (from box centre) | 17 standing, 12 crouched | `PM_Duck` (17, and 12 − 18 = −6 mid-crouch) |
| Crouch time | 0.4 s on the ground, instant in the air | `PM_Duck` (0.6 = 1 − 0.4, spline scale 2.5) |
| Shift-walk | × 0.52 → 130 u/s with a knife | client cvar `cl_movespeedkey` (`client.so`) |
| Footsteps | only at 150 u/s or faster | `PM_UpdateStepSound` |
| Ladder climb / jump off | 200 / 270 u/s | `PM_LadderMove` |
| Swimming | 0.8 × max speed, sink 60 u/s, swim up 100 u/s | `PM_WaterMove`, `PM_Jump` |
| Fall damage | (speed − 500) × 100/600 × 1.25 HP; lethal ≈ 980 u/s | `FlPlayerFallDamage @a5200`, `CBasePlayer::PostThink` |

Weapon move speeds (AK 221, AWP 210, ...) are in `docs/RULES.md`.

## Doors

`sim/src/doors.rs`: `func_door` (sliding) and `func_door_rotating`, plus
`trigger_multiple` zones that open named doors (de_nuke's glass doors).
GoldSrc rules: named doors open only from their trigger, unnamed ones on touch,
use-only doors with E; rotating doors swing away from the opener; a closing
door that hits a player goes back; `wait`, `speed`, `lip`, toggle and one-way
come from the map.

## Not done yet

- Water jump-out (climbing out of water onto a ledge, `PM_CheckWaterJump`).
- Footstep interval is 300 ms ⚠ (HL convention, not yet read from `PM_UpdateStepSound`).
- Doors don't push players and have no sounds; buttons and breakables come with weapons.
- Ladder face direction is taken from the ladder box's thin side ⚠ (fine for the
  stock maps' straight ladders).

## Tests

- `cargo test -p sim`: flat-floor checks for landing, run speed, friction,
  45-unit jump, crouch speed and timing, bunny-hop cap, fall damage, shift-walk,
  and determinism.
- `sim/tests/maps.rs` (skipped if CS 1.6 isn't installed): every spawn on
  de_dust2, de_inferno, de_nuke and de_train lands, then runs and jumps without
  getting stuck; nuke's glass doors open from their trigger and close again;
  inferno's rotating door opens on touch; all 16 de_train ladders can be climbed.
- `cargo test -p client`: a rendered door sits exactly where its collision is.
```
